# Modifications

This is gpui 0.2.2 from crates.io, changed by qol-tools:

- `src/elements/text.rs`: each measure of a text element truncates a copy of its runs, so a narrow measure no longer shortens what a later, wider layout draws. Zed fixed the same bug upstream in zed-industries/zed#45122.
- `src/text_system.rs`: `line_clamp` counts each hard line break as a line. It counted only wrapped lines, so a clamped text with line breaks drew every paragraph past its clamp, and a two-line toast detail holding a multi-paragraph report overflowed the card. This is an upstream candidate for zed-industries/zed.
- `src/taffy.rs`: the grid repeat names its float literals `f32`, as Zed does upstream, so newer compilers do not reject the fallback to `f32`.
- `src/window.rs`: when the platform reports a resize or move while the app is already borrowed, the window reads its new bounds once that update returns instead of dropping them, and several reports before then share one deferred read. qol code sets a native window frame synchronously inside an update, and gpui used to keep the stale viewport and scale and log `RefCell already borrowed`.
- `src/platform/linux/x11/window.rs`: a new window is created at its requested origin (no 2 px shift) and WM_NORMAL_HINTS carries that origin and size as user-specified with static gravity, so Muffin and other window managers map it there instead of placing it and moving it after the first map, and a restored inner bounds lands exactly. Upstream gpui still sets only the minimum size; this is an upstream candidate for zed-industries/zed.
- The `examples` and `docs` folders and the `[[example]]` targets are removed.
- `src/app/test_context.rs` and `src/platform/test/window.rs`: expose the fake window handle and add simulated moves so workspace regression tests can deliver resize/move callbacks during an app update. The tests cover deferred bounds, coalescing, subsequent immediate updates, and closing a window before deferred work runs.
- `src/platform/windows/keyboard.rs`: the AltGr layout list adds Danish, Italian, Brazilian Portuguese, Icelandic, Belgian French, Swiss German, Swiss French, Croatian, Estonian, Latvian, Lithuanian, Greek and Bulgarian, so `@ $ { [ ] }` type on a Danish layout.
- `src/platform/windows/direct_write.rs`: when a family name matches no font by its weight-stretch-style (WSS) family name, the lookup retries with the WSS name of a font whose typographic family has that name. It prefers the WSS name equal to the typographic name, otherwise the face closest to the requested weight, stretch and style. A font whose faces carry a WSS family that differs from its typographic family could not load by its typographic name, because DirectWrite's `GetMatchingFonts` only matches the WSS name. This is an upstream candidate for zed-industries/zed.
- `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: `activate` sends its synthetic Alt press and release only while Alt is up. A held Alt already lets the process take the foreground, and the injected release made a hold-to-switch picker opened by Alt+Tab read Alt as released and close at once.
- `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: a window opened hidden keeps the on-screen position the app gave it when it is first activated. gpui used to re-apply the placement it stored at creation, so a hidden preview that qol moved next to the cursor jumped back to where it was created on its first show. A window opened hidden also takes its placement's frame at creation, as a shown window does: it was created with its content size as its frame size, so a hidden panel kept a content area smaller than it asked for.
- `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: a new window is created at its requested bounds, converted with its target display's scale, so it starts on that display at that display's DPI. gpui created it on the primary display and converted the bounds with the primary display's scale, so a window opened on a display with another scale landed at the wrong origin and Windows grew it by the ratio of the two scales when it moved there.
- `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: the window frame offsets keep the measured left and top insets, so a window placed or resized at client bounds puts its client exactly there. gpui split the frame evenly between top and bottom, but a window without a native title bar has a 1 to 2 px top inset and an 8 to 11 px bottom one, so every placement and resize moved the client up 3 to 4 px and a remembered window crept upward on each reopen.
- `src/platform/windows/window.rs`, `src/platform/windows/events.rs`: a window gpui has dropped no longer calls back into gpui. gpui destroys a dropped window later on its executor, and what reached it in between (hit tests, key releases, paints, the deactivation sent while it is destroyed) was handed to a window gpui no longer had, so every closed window logged `window not found` errors.
- `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: `activate` logs `SetActiveWindow` and `SetFocus` only when they fail. Both return the previously active or focused window, so a window activated while the app had none logged an error with the code for success.
- `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: `resize` keeps the window's activation and stacking. gpui resized with a plain `SetWindowPos`, which also raises and activates the window, so a resize could take the keyboard from another window: shrinking the hidden shot preview after it opened the editor left the editor without keys. This is an upstream candidate for zed-industries/zed.
- `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: a window opened visible with `focus: false` is shown without being activated, as Zed does upstream since zed-industries/zed#61411. gpui showed every new window with `SW_SHOWNORMAL`, which activates it, so a toast took the keyboard from the window the user was in: the tray's "Screenshot saved" toast took focus from the shot preview that opened with it.
- `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: a `PopUp` window is created topmost, as its documentation promises and as macOS does by raising it to the pop-up window level. gpui gave it only the tool window style, so a toast opened behind a maximized window and was never seen. This is an upstream candidate for zed-industries/zed.
- `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: `activate` taps an unassigned key between its synthetic Alt press and release. A lone Alt reaches the window that still has the keyboard and puts it into menu mode, so the first Settings window after the tray started left Notepad behind it showing its menu key tips, and the next letter typed into Notepad opened a menu instead. This is an upstream candidate for zed-industries/zed.
- `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: a `Floating` window is owned by the app's active window when it opens, as X11 makes it transient for the focused window and Wayland gives it that parent. gpui opened it as an unowned app window, so qol's color wheel added a second, untitled window to the taskbar button and nothing kept it above the settings window it belongs to. This is an upstream candidate for zed-industries/zed.
- `src/platform/windows/system_settings.rs`, `src/platform/windows/events.rs`, `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: a window asks the taskbar whether it auto-hides only once it is maximized, and again after the work area changes, instead of each time a window is created. The question waits on Explorer, so while Explorer's taskbar hung, no window could open until Explorer recovered. This is an upstream candidate for zed-industries/zed.
- `src/platform/windows/events.rs`, `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: text typed as Unicode packets (`VK_PACKET`), which input tools send through `SendInput` with `KEYEVENTF_UNICODE`, reaches a window without a text input handler as key-down keystrokes, the way typed keys do. gpui handed that text only to an input handler, so views that read keystrokes, such as qol's search fields, never saw it.
- `src/platform/windows/events.rs`, `src/platform/windows/keyboard.rs`: a keystroke's `key_char` is the text the key types, as on Linux and macOS. The space key types a space, and a dead key types nothing until the key after it completes the character. gpui gave the space key no `key_char` and gave a dead key its accent, so views that read `key_char`, such as qol's search fields, dropped every space and typed `café` as `caf'é`.
